commit.message:
feat(post): a PathPilot (LinuxCNC) lathe post

assets/posts/tormach-lathe.cps, registered as "Tormach PathPilot Lathe"
(BUILTINS + LATHE_POSTS; the lathe default stays Fanuc Lathe). Specced
from the LinuxCNC G-code reference and lathe page and Tormach's public
PathPilot lathe programming pages: G7 diameter X, G18, G20/G21 from the
machine, G95 per-rev feeds, G97 / G96 D<max> S, G30 then T0101 (no M6),
G2/G3 with radius I, threading as one merged G33 Z K per pass or - with
the Threading option - the one-block LinuxCNC G76 P Z I J R1 K Q0 H,
drilling on centre as plain moves with a G4 dwell in seconds. Refused by
name: tapping, back-bore, off-axis holes, G76 records it cannot state
exactly (compound infeed, finish allowance, pull-out, unequal rungs,
internal / -X threads), tool numbers outside T01-T99, nose-radius comp.
The UI threading picker shows for both lathe posts.

Goldens: nc/tormach-lathe/{turning,thread_g33,thread_g76,axial_drill}
_{mm,inch}.nc, pinned by lathe_post_tormach.rs with a LinuxCNC syntax
check over every program; conformance lists the new post.

Refs #612

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01CUsqDAgjpiZbXSvmXLvdmL

fix(turning): threads cut right-hand toward the chuck by default; the hand is stated, never dropped

Threading passes ran toward +Z (away from the chuck) and the Fanuc Lathe
post wrote them under M03, dropping the CL arc sense: every thread came
out left-hand. Now:

- Threading carries a `hand` (Right default, Left) - OpParams, project
  file (optional key, absent reads right), EditOperationParams (undoable),
  the Passes tab ("Right hand" / "Left hand"), and MCP via the params DTO.
- The engine runs every pass toward the chuck (top lattice point down);
  the hand sets the half-turns' sense (RH clockwise seen from +Z = M03).
- ThreadCycle carries the hand; is_sane holds the passes to it. The stream
  states THREAD ... HAND and PARAM SpindleDirection reverse when the
  passes need M04; a script must declare threadHands to receive one.
- fanuc-lathe.cps writes M03/M04 from it, refuses a G32 half-turn turning
  against the spindle, and refuses a G76 record whose hand and direction
  need the other spindle (or that states no hand).
- thread_hand_warnings convicts a helix of the wrong hand as a gouge.
- Golden thread_g76.nc: G76 now starts at Z14 and ends at Z8.

Fixes #629

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01CUsqDAgjpiZbXSvmXLvdmL

fix(turning): lathe posts write the tool's control point for its orientation, not the nose centre

The turning kernels' CL is the insert's nose-circle centre, and both
lathe posts wrote it raw under G40 - so a Ø19.05 finish posted X20.65
(2r oversize) and a face at Z0 posted Z0.8. Under G40 the control
drives the tool's control point, the imaginary tip the operator touches
off on (LinuxCNC Lathe User Information 7.1).

- Turning inserts and boring bars carry a lathe tool orientation
  (LinuxCNC's 1-9 chart, camcraft_tools::orientation; unstated reads as
  the kind's default: 2 for a turning insert, 3 for a boring bar),
  editable in the tool editor (applied through ChangeTool, undoable),
  saved additively in the project and tool library.
- One shared conversion in the post layer (post::nose_tip, called once
  from posting::op_streams): the nose-centre path moved by
  r * tip_offset(q) - the exact compensated control-point path on
  diameters, faces, tapers and arcs. The cached toolpath, the verifier
  and the stock sim keep the nose centre.
- An orientation whose nose cannot present the cut's contacts is
  refused by name with the list that fits (PathPilot's own reading).
- fanuc-lathe.cps: the "nose centre" stream claim is gone; G40 stays,
  the tool note names the orientation (PARAM ToolOrientation).
- Fanuc Lathe goldens regenerated: facing and profile rough/finish
  moved by (-2r in X, -r in Z).

Fixes #630

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01CUsqDAgjpiZbXSvmXLvdmL

fix(turning): grooving and parting blades post their touched-off corner

The blade kernels' CL is the middle of the tip edge (each plunge at a
band centre), and the lathe posts wrote it raw - but a grooving/parting
blade is touched off on a corner (LinuxCNC Lathe User Information 4.2),
so grooves and part-offs landed width/2 off in Z.

- A blade's lathe orientation (#630's field) names its touched-off
  corner: 1 the +Z corner, 2 the -Z corner (the default, 4.2's example),
  6 the width centre (9 read as 6). Edited in the tool editor through
  ChangeTool (undoable); old blades read as the default.
- posting::nose shifts a GrooveRough/GrooveFinish/Part path by
  side * width/2 in Z through the shared post::nose_tip conversion; no
  corner-radius term (the imaginary tip of a rounded corner is the sharp
  corner). An ID/face code (3, 4, 5, 7, 8) is refused by name.
- The cached path, verifier, stock sim and gouge laws keep the centre.
- Fanuc Lathe groove_part.nc regenerated: plunges and clearance move
  -w/2 in Z (GT-0200: -1, GT-0300: -1.5), tool note names ORIENTATION 2.

Fixes #641

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(machines): the built-in Lathe's X reaches a little past centre for facing

The lathe posts now write the tool's control point: a facing pass that
faces clean to centre puts the nose centre on X0 and the orientation-2
tip at -r (X-1.6 on diameter for r0.8), which the one-sided 0..320 band
could not reach. The built-in Lathe's X band becomes -2.5..320 (Ø-5):
3.1x the catalog's deepest control point, and room for an ISO r2.4
nose. lathe_x_stays_a_centreline_band pins the new floor; a facing pass
to centre fits the band, and a centreline at X-10 still refuses by name.

Refs #630

fix(turning): facing approaches at rapid and lifts off the face before retracting

The facing kernel opened with a plunge FEED from wherever the turret
parked (no commanded approach) and retracted each pass radially at the
Z just cut, dragging the nose back across the fresh face.

- The path now starts on the spindle axis on the clearance plane (the
  lathe's reading of the mill kernels' origin start) and its first move
  is a rapid out to the clearance point (rho_clear, clearance): the
  posted program's first motion after the tool call is G00 to it. The
  approach is judged by the meridian rapid law (#103); a clearance plane
  inside the bar convicts it and blocks the post.
- Every pass lifts the nose off its face along the axis by LIFT
  (0.2 mm, held to half the stepdown, which keeps the lifted rapid in
  air the ladder already cleared) before the radial rapid out.

Fanuc Lathe facing golden regenerated: G00 X13 Z25 before the first
plunge, and each "G00 X13 Z<s>" retract becomes "G00 X-1.6 Z<s+0.2>"
then "G00 X13 Z<s+0.2>".

feat(post): the PathPilot lathe post takes the stated thread hand and the tool's control point

Adapts tormach-lathe.cps to the merged lathe stream (#629, #630, #641,
#632) and fixes the two post defects the Hub kit build recorded.

- threadHands = true: M3, or M4 (with a mount-for-M4 note) under PARAM
  SpindleDirection reverse; each G33 half-turn's arc sense is checked
  against the section's spindle and a mismatch refused by name; a G76
  record whose hand and Z direction disagree with the spindle refused.
  G33/G76 cut from the top toward EndZ (the chuck), as the stream does.
- The stream point is the tool's control point: the tool note states
  ORIENTATION n; goldens shift X-1.6 Z-0.8 for the r0.8 orientation-2
  insert (finish now on the Ø7 neck and the Z2 shoulder).
- G33 K is one number per thread (the THREAD record's lead), half-turns
  merge within a 2.5 um lattice allowance - a 12 TPI lead no longer
  splits a pass into blocks with different K.
- G76 words on the control's grid: I J K computed once in grid steps,
  root rounded outward (never deeper than the minor), J shallower; the
  diameter/height checks allow the stream lattice (2.5 um) so a legal
  cycle is not refused. Word order P Z I J K R Q H (PathPilot's
  conversational order); R1/Q0/H from the record; no D (undocumented in
  LinuxCNC's and Tormach's G76).
- Suites split: lathe_post_tormach (turning/drill/dialect) and
  lathe_post_tormach_thread (G33/G76/hand), fixtures in
  tests/tormach_lathe_support.
